pull_request.title: prove: remove paging layout axiom and refactor architecture specs
pull_request.body:
## Remove the paging-layout axiom

Remove `PagingConstsTrait::axiom_current_paging_consts_hardcoded` and all of its uses. The layout facts required by the current page-table owner model become explicit proof obligations of `PageTableConfig`, proved by the user and kernel configurations. Index-range proofs derive their bounds from the generic paging configuration. This replaces an unchecked assumption with obligations that Verus checks for each implementation.
pull_request.bodyHTML:
Remove the paging-layout axiom

Remove PagingConstsTrait::axiom_current_paging_consts_hardcoded and all of its uses. The layout facts required by the current page-table owner model become explicit proof obligations of PageTableConfig, proved by the user and kernel configurations. Index-range proofs derive their bounds from the generic paging configuration. This replaces an unchecked assumption with obligations that Verus checks for each implementation.

The new change just moved the three hardcoded constant postconditions from PagingConstsTrait to PageTableConfig, I have several problems:

  • Since this constraint is purely related to the paging constants, if you still need them, you should retain them in PagingConstsTrait::lemma_paging_consts_requirements.

Please let AI check whether this constraint will cause issues when we try to verify the ARM arch introduced in later Asterinas versions and the IOMMU. If there are no problems, then I will be okay with this.

issue_comments.body_html:
The new change just moved the three hardcoded constant postconditions from PagingConstsTrait to PageTableConfig, I have several problems:

  • Since this constraint is purely related to the paging constants, if you still need them, you should retain them in PagingConstsTrait::lemma_paging_consts_requirements.
  • The current proof exploits the fact that x86/riscv/loongarch share the same BASE_PAGE_SIZE, PTE_SIZE and NR_LEVELS. Please let AI check whether this constraint will cause issues when we try to verify the ARM arch introduced in later Asterinas versions and the IOMMU. I checked the latest Asterinas main branch. ARM currently uses a 4 KiB base page, 4 page-table levels, and 8-byte page-table entries, matching x86, RISC-V, and LoongArch. So this constraint does not appear to cause an issue for the current ARM configuration.

However, I don’t think these equalities can be moved into the general PagingConstsTrait::lemma_paging_consts_requirements postconditions, because IOMMU also implements PagingConstsTrait and uses 3 page-table levels, which do not match the architecture constants. The architecture-specific PagingConsts implementation should establish these equalities where needed, while the generic trait requirements remain valid for IOMMU’s paging constants.

review_comments.body:
Yes, the current x86-64, RISC-V, and LoongArch CPU page-table configurations share the same layout and user/kernel top-level index ranges, so these definitions yield the same values.

I moved these two lemmas into `vaddr_range_proofs.rs` to avoid duplicating the proofs across architectures and to keep them alongside the page-table specifications they describe. They establish bounds for the concrete `UserPtConfig` and `KernelPtConfig`, combining architecture-provided paging constants with the user/kernel top-level index ranges.

This also removes the architecture specification modules' direct dependency on these page-table specifications.

review_comments.body:
The intention is to separate the architecture-independent model from its current-target instantiation. `model.rs` provides a generic lemma over `ArchAddressSpaceModel`, while `lemma_paddr_to_vaddr_properties` in `arch/mod.rs` instantiates it with `CurrentArch` and connects the modeled conversion to the executable `paddr_to_vaddr`.

I kept this lemma to expose the shared property at the model level and make the current-target proof explicitly reuse it. Its purpose is to preserve this separation, even though the proof body is empty.
